assembly_instructions: Built as an open flow-network diagram at conceptual 1x scale (meters), laid out left-to-right so capital reads as moving from sources to sinks. (1) Lay base_platform as a thin rooted concrete floor plate and frame its rim with the four perimeter kerb members. (2) Stand the three liquidity-pool tanks on it at x=-5 (z=+2.2, 0, -2.2), drop a fluid-level disk into each to show uneven reserves, cap each with a torus rim, and mount an external glass sight-tube with a float bead on the +Z face so the reserve level reads from outside. (3) Build the AMM as an open chamber: set amm_core floor deck, raise the -X wall (amm_leftwall) and -Z wall (amm_backwall), stand the two front corner posts, run the central amm_shaft up the middle, tie the posts and inflow wall together with three top rails, and add two diagonal knee-braces so the rotor frame is fully triangulated; leave the +X and +Z faces open so the interior shows. (4) Place the two reserve columns inside — tall reserve_x and short reserve_y — to display the x·y=k invariant. (5) Route the three inflow pipes into amm_leftwall, thick for ETH/USDC and medium for DAI. (6) Cap the shaft with the rotor disk and its two crossed paddles. (7) Run pipe_amm_fee from the AMM right into fee_junction_main (carried on junction_main_post, topped by a handwheel split-valve); branch a thin pipe to fee_junction_lp (on junction_lp_post, also valve-topped) and a thick pipe to the vault. (8) Return the thin LP-fee pipe along z=-2.6 back into the USDC pool, carried on three short steel brackets down to the platform, closing the loop. (9) Build the lending vault as a cutaway: rear shell, floor, one side wall with a corner gusset, a front corner post and a top lintel framing the open face, with three stacked capital ingots and a borrower-ledger pillar inside, framed by the circular vault door. (10) Feed the vault output into the yield_manifold header (carried on two posts), wrap a brass saddle collar at each of the five tap points, and fan it out through five thin pipes to four white recipient wallets and one taller brass protocol-treasury vault resting on a shelf supported by two legs.

info.summary: A flow-network model of how capital moves through a decentralized-finance system: liquidity pools feed an automated market maker, which routes fees and lent capital through junctions and a vault to a yield-distribution manifold. It visualizes uneven flow magnitudes as pipe diameters, reads reserve levels through external sight-gauges, and exposes the AMM and vault interiors as cutaways.
info.description: Decentralized finance (DeFi) replaces banks and brokers with smart contracts on public blockchains. Capital is supplied by liquidity providers into pooled reserves; an automated market maker (AMM) prices swaps against those reserves using a constant-product invariant x · y = k, so a trade that removes one asset must add the other to keep the product constant. Each swap charges a fee (0.30% on Uniswap v2), which is split between liquidity providers and, optionally, the protocol treasury. This model renders that pipeline as plumbing: three liquidity-pool tanks (ETH, DAI, USDC) feed a central AMM chamber through pipes whose thickness encodes flow size, and each tank carries an external glass sight-gauge whose float bead shows the pooled reserve. The AMM is built as an open frame so the two reserve columns embodying x · y = k are visible inside. The AMM output passes a fee-split junction that branches capital toward a lending vault and recycles LP fees back to the pools along a return line carried on steel brackets. The vault is shown as a cutaway holding stacked capital ingots and a borrower ledger; its interest-bearing output enters a yield-distribution manifold, collared with brass saddle taps, that fans through thin pipes to four small LP recipient wallets and one taller protocol-treasury vault. Total value locked across DeFi has ranged roughly $50–180 billion since 2021.

parts.name: Flow-network floor plate
parts.role: Thin rooted concrete floor plate of the diagram; all tanks, the AMM, vault, kerb frame and support posts stand on it.

parts.name: ETH liquidity-pool tank
parts.role: Holds the pooled ETH reserve supplied by liquidity providers and feeds the largest inflow to the AMM.

parts.name: DAI liquidity-pool tank
parts.role: Holds the pooled DAI stablecoin reserve, contributing the smaller of the three AMM inflows.

parts.name: USDC liquidity-pool tank
parts.role: Holds the pooled USDC reserve, feeds the AMM and receives the recycled LP-fee return line.

parts.name: ETH tank top rim

parts.role: Reinforcing rim marking the open fill mouth of the DAI tank.

parts.name: USDC reserve fluid level

parts.name: USDC gauge float bead
parts.role: Float bead riding mid-height in the USDC sight-gauge, marking a moderate pooled reserve.

parts.name: DAI inflow pipe (medium)

parts.name: USDC inflow pipe (thick)
parts.role: Thick conduit carrying the large USDC capital flow into the AMM chamber wall.

parts.role: Floor deck of the open automated-market-maker chamber; supports the reserve columns and roots the AMM frame.

parts.name: AMM chamber inflow wall
parts.role: The -X wall of the AMM chamber; the three inflow pipes penetrate it to deliver pooled capital.

parts.name: AMM chamber back wall
parts.role: The -Z wall of the AMM chamber; the +X and +Z faces are left open so the reserves are visible.

parts.role: Front corner column carrying the rotor deck and bracing the open -Z face of the AMM chamber.

parts.role: Top rail along Z tying the two AMM front corner posts together, framing the open +X face beneath the rotor.

parts.name: AMM frame top rail (+Z side)
parts.role: Top side rail running from the +Z front post back to the inflow wall, completing the AMM chamber frame.

parts.name: AMM frame top rail (-Z side)
parts.role: Top side rail running from the -Z front post back to the inflow wall, completing the AMM chamber frame.

parts.name: AMM frame knee-brace (+Z)
parts.role: Diagonal knee-brace triangulating the +Z front corner post to its top side rail so the rotor deck is stiffly carried.

parts.name: AMM frame knee-brace (-Z)
parts.role: Diagonal knee-brace triangulating the -Z front corner post to its top side rail so the rotor deck is stiffly carried.

parts.name: AMM rotor shaft
parts.role: Central vertical shaft transmitting rebalancing motion from the chamber floor up to the constant-product rotor.

parts.name: Asset-X reserve column (large)
parts.role: Tall interior reserve column for asset x; its height versus reserve_y embodies the x·y=k constant-product invariant.

parts.name: Asset-Y reserve column (small)
parts.role: Short interior reserve column for asset y; depleted relative to reserve_x so their product x·y stays constant.

parts.name: Constant-product rotor disk
parts.role: Rotating hub atop the AMM shaft that drives the rebalancing paddles as the two reserves shift.

parts.name: Rebalancing paddle A
parts.role: Mixer blade representing one side of the x·y=k rebalancing action as a swap executes.

parts.name: Rebalancing paddle B
parts.role: Crossed mixer blade representing the opposing side of the constant-product rebalance.

parts.name: AMM output pipe (thick)
parts.role: Thick conduit carrying swapped capital plus accrued fees out of the AMM toward the fee-split junction.

parts.name: Main fee-split junction box
parts.role: Branch point that splits AMM output between the lending vault and the LP-fee return path.

parts.name: Main junction split-valve wheel
parts.role: Brass handwheel valve on top of the main junction setting the fee-split ratio between the vault feed and the LP return.

parts.name: Main junction support post
parts.role: Steel pedestal carrying the main fee-split junction at AMM flow height down to the base plate.

parts.name: LP-fee split junction box
parts.role: Secondary junction that routes the liquidity-provider share of fees back toward the pools.

parts.name: LP junction split-valve wheel

parts.name: LP junction support post
parts.role: Steel pedestal carrying the LP-fee junction down to the base plate.

parts.name: LP-fee return pipe (thin)
parts.role: Thin return line recycling earned LP fees back into the USDC pool, closing the capital loop.
